summary: Max Oidtmann works in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology. Educated at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard under Mark Elliott, he held posts at Georgetown University, Georgetown University in Qatar, and became a professor at the University of Munich around 2020.

Philosopher Max Scheler studied at the universities of Munich, Berlin, and Jena. He held academic posts at Jena (~1899–1907), Munich (~1907–1910), Göttingen (~1910–1911), and the University of Cologne (~1919–1928).

Max Walleser worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Geneva, and Erlangen-Nuremberg, and served at Heidelberg University as Privatdozent in 1911 and extraordinary professor of Indian philology from 1918 to 1936.
May Oung studied at the University of Cambridge from around 1904 to 1907. Active in history and archaeology, he founded the Burma Research Society in 1910.

Historian Maya Jasanoff studied at Harvard College, the University of Cambridge, Yale University, and Harvard University. She held a post at the University of Virginia (~2003–2009) before becoming a history professor at Harvard around 2009.

Mayumi Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She held posts as a lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2011–2013) and as a specially appointed associate professor at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

McKim Marriott worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University and the University of Chicago under Clyde Kluckhohn, later serving as professor of anthropology and social sciences at the University of Chicago from 1955 to 1998.

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having earned an MA at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and a PhD at Nanjing University. Publications from 2008 attest his teaching posts at Colombo, Buddhist and Pali University, and PGIPBS.
Medhani studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.
Megan Bryson, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, studied at Stanford University. Publications from 2017 attest her affiliation with the University of Tennessee.
Megumu Honda, active in Indology and Buddhist studies, studied under Johannes Rahder, Paul Tedesco, and Rulon Wells. A 1996 publication attests him as a professor at Doho University.

Mei Ching Hsuan works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed a PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger and Dieter Schuh, and is attested as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies in 2026.
Meiji Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962). Publications attest his post as professor at Ryukoku University in 1963 and 2007.

Meinrad Scheller, a linguist and Indologist, studied under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch at the University of Zurich and the University of Paris. He held professorships at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (1975).
Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fo Guang University, earning a Master of Arts under Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Melissa R. Kerin is a scholar in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter.
Melvin Pötzsch works in linguistics and Indology. Publications from 2026 attest his positions as a research fellow and academic staff member (Wiss. Mitarbeiter) at the University of Marburg.

Melvyn C. Goldstein works in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Washington, and was a professor in the Department of Anthropology at Case Western Reserve University from 1968 to 2002.

Philosopher Merab Mamardashvili studied philosophy at Moscow University (~1949–1954). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).

Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (attested 1980), having also studied under Kathryn A. Cissell.
